Earth is gone, swallowed by a savage alien realm. Humanity is prey, starting with nothing but thatch and a prayer. But Wren Vance isn't panicking. Team up? Pass. Crippling social anxiety. Eat flavorless rations? Hell no. A girl's gotta eat. Armed with a bizarre family relic, Wren unlocks a daily talent lottery. Her routine? Wake up, spin the wheel, and grind. While others freeze in mud huts, Wren lounges in a climate-controlled villa, plating gourmet dinners. While they flee monsters, she's taming beasts and building her second fortress. Dominating the leaderboards attracts jealous raiders. When they threaten to hunt her down, Wren drops a single broadcast to the world: "Looking for my coordinates? Come on over. I've got a one-way ticket to the afterlife waiting just for you."
Chapter 1 Global Survival
'Where in the world am I?' Wren Vance wondered, blinking at the endless wasteland stretching out before her.
She stood there in cartoon pajamas and fluffy panda slippers, a bizarre backpack slung over her shoulders.
She had just survived a brutal college semester and finally flown back home for the summer.
It had barely been a day. She missed out on the loaded nachos and deep-dish pizza she had been craving for months.
'Did I really just wake up and teleport to another dimension? Maybe this is just a super realistic fever dream,' she thought, rubbing her eyes.
Looking totally out of place in the barren dirt, Wren bounced the mysterious backpack that had materialized out of thin air.
She was just about to take it off to check inside when a massive holographic screen popped up right in front of her face.
A glowing little orb bounced playfully across the screen. It let out a series of giggles before a childish yet incredibly grating voice echoed through the air.
\[Welcome to the Survival Game, residents of Earth! To my dear players in The Central Federation Sector 47: please adjust your attitudes and read the following game rules carefully.\]
"A survival game?" Wren muttered out loud, furrowing her brow as she locked eyes on the glowing sphere.
\[1\. Player Selection: The player pool consists of able-bodied Earthlings aged 15 to 60. Participation is mandatory and irreversible. If you die in the game, you die for real.\
\
\[2\. Beginner's Grace Period: This phase lasts for exactly three days. Players take 90% less damage during this time. Gather supplies fast. After the grace period, difficulty will spike from Normal to Hard, and system quests will begin.\
\
\[3\. Exploration Boundaries: Novices must stick to their starting zones. Wandering into unreleased Mist-Shrouded Maps will immediately cancel your beginner protection.\
\
\[4\. Loot and Combat: Go out and explore. Some areas have random loot chests. Killing monsters gives you a chance at rare item drops. Novice Tip: Trust absolutely nothing, including the plants.\
\
\[5\. Chat Etiquette: Keep it clean. During the grace period, World Chat is limited to three messages a day. Private messages and post-grace period chats are completely unlimited. Spamming is banned.\
\
\[6\. System Updates: Pay close attention to system announcements, leaderboards, and quests.\
\
\[7\. Safehouse: Your starting backpack contains the basic materials needed to build a beginner Safehouse. Find a good spot and establish your base.\
\
\[8\. Inventory: A Novice Starter Pack has been deposited into your bag. Open your system panel to read the rest of the guide.\]\
\
The moment the orb finished talking, it lunged forward and flattened itself against the screen like a squashed bug. Its voice spiked into a piercing shriek.\
\
\[To all my dear players, the Survival Game starts right now! Good luck surviving the novice phase. Make sure you stay alive!\]\
\
A second later, the giant screen shattered into a burst of starlight. The light swirled together, forming a solid silver ring that snapped perfectly onto Wren's right index finger.\
\
She raised her hand in total disbelief. 'A silver ring out of literally nowhere?' she pondered, staring at her hand.\
\
Remembering what the annoying orb had said about a system panel, she focused her mind. Instantly, the holographic screen projected right out of the ring.\
\
The world chat channel was already scrolling so fast that the text was a total blur.\
\
Wren pressed her finger against the screen, pausing the feed to catch a few of the messages.\
\
\[What the hell is going on? Are aliens invading us?\] typed one panicked player.\
\
\[A survival game? The graphics are insane. Is this a secret VR beta test?\] asked another.\
\
\[Bro, let me out of here! I am highly allergic to grass!\]\
\
\[Oh baby, it is my time to shine! I am totally the main character and I am going to rule this world!\]\
\
\[SOS, please send a tutorial on how to log out.\]\
\
Nobody had a single clue about their current nightmare.\
\
Deciding that reading the chaotic spam was a massive waste of time, Wren manually closed the chat and tapped on her personal profile.\
\
\[Player Profile: Wren Vance\
\
\[Age: 22\
\
\[Stamina: 4 9Replenish soon. (Dropping below 2 causes sluggishness.)\
\
\[Health Points: 10\
\
\[Strength: 7\
\
\[Willpower: 20\
\
\[Luck: 12\
\
\[(Note: Attributes can be upgraded)\]\
\
Staring at her pathetic four points of stamina, Wren could only curse her awful luck.\
\
She woke up early and immediately got dragged into this bizarre place without a bite of breakfast.\
\
Still, she had to look on the bright side. If she had been teleported while sleeping in bed, she wouldn't even have her panda slippers right now.\
\
Spotting a quick toggle button in the top right corner to hide her stats and location, she activated it immediately.\
\
'Better to keep a low profile,' she reminded herself, tapping the screen. 'Showing your hand on day one is just asking to get robbed.'\
\
Right below her basic stats, the profile featured a row of other tabs: Friends, Quests, Announcements, Leaderboards, Achievements, Guide, and Trading Post.\
\
Unlike the rest, the Quests, Leaderboards, and Trading Post buttons were completely grayed out. Tapping them simply triggered a pop-up warning.\
\
\[Unlocks after the Beginner's Grace Period.\]\
\
Since she was still stuck in the novice phase, most of the tabs were completely empty. Finding no other useful information, she simply closed the interface.\
\
With the system exploration out of the way, Wren instinctively reached up to rub the crystal core hanging around her neck. Her fingers grasped empty air.\
\
Panic instantly flared in her chest. That necklace was the only thing she had left from her biological parents, tucked inside her swaddling clothes when she was dropped off at the foster home.\
\
Grace Lane, her old foster mom, always told her about the letter left with the baby blankets.\
\
Her parents claimed they had hit rock bottom and couldn't afford to raise her, praying a good Samaritan would take her in.\
\
The crystal core itself was nothing fancy. It was a cloudy, earth-toned, crescent-shaped geode filled with dull impurities that looked completely worthless.\
\
Grace had tied it on a simple leather cord, and it had rested against Wren's chest for over two decades.\
\
Whenever Wren was deep in thought, she would instinctively trace the worn ridges of the stone.\
\
Realizing it was missing, she frantically patted down her pajama pockets. Empty.\
\
Her only hope was the strange backpack strapped to her shoulders.\
\
'Maybe the bag automatically sucked the crystal core into its inventory?' she hoped, pulling the bag off her back.\
\
Opening the backpack revealed a digital grid of 25 storage slots. Inside, she found the Novice Starter Pack, Wood Plank x50, Dry Hay x60, Iron Nails x15, and sitting perfectly safe in the last occupied slot, her Crystal Core.\
\
Wren Vance hurriedly pulled the crystal out of her bag. The second it hit the open air, a voice bursting with static crackled directly into her brain.\
\
\[Bzz... bzzzt...\] the robotic voice buzzed. \[Race: Human. Faction: None. Bind item?\]\
\
Wren blinked in total confusion. 'Bind? Bind what? This core?' she wondered.\
\
Before she could even process the prompt, the system just made the call for her.\
\
\[Binding complete,\] it chimed. \[Detecting critical physical condition. Roll for a starting talent immediately?\]\
\
She did not need to be a genius to figure this out. It was painfully obvious the crystal core her parents left her was top-tier loot.\
\
Plus, she had already hit rock bottom. Stranded in an alien world and completely solo, things literally could not get any worse.\
\
Gritting her teeth, she sent a mental command. 'Roll it.'\
\
A retro loot box covered in bright red and yellow polka dots popped straight out of the core.\
\
It rapidly expanded into a neat twelve-inch cube.\
\
Blinding golden light poured from the top slot, making it completely impossible to peek inside.\
\
Stepping up, Wren plunged her hand right into the box. 'Come on, RNGesus, give me something broken!'\
\
Her fingers brushed against a smooth little sphere. She snatched it up and yanked her hand out. The bright light in her palm instantly melted into her skin, triggering another alert.\
\
The system announced: \[Talent Unlocked: Seeker's Sight\
\
\[Talent Tier: Level 1\
\
\[Detection Radius: 500 yards\]\
\
\[Upgrade Requirement: 30 Willpower\
\
\[Talent Breakdown: Perception scales with tier and Willpower. Higher Willpower expands range and visual clarity. Nothing within your radius can hide. Note: Evolvable.\]\
\
A wave of crisp, refreshing energy washed over her. Wren's mind instantly sharpened.\
\
A holographic mini-map unfurled in her vision, pinging the surrounding terrain with various little icons.\
\
Her eyes practically bugged out of her head. 'Holy crap. I am gonna farm loot chests so incredibly fast now!'\
\
Chapter 2 Establishing the Safehouse\
\
Knowing she could instantly pinpoint loot chests and resources, Wren was itching to start scavenging.\
\
She stared at the crystal core in her hand and gave it two loud, enthusiastic smacks. Holding it up against the sunlight, she admired its new look.\
\
Compared to its original form back on Earth, the core had undergone a total makeover. The dull, muddy exterior was completely gone, replaced by a smooth, warm amber base.\
\
Up close, faint, glittering currents of light swirled deep inside.\
\
Even better, the hovering item description now read: \[Enigma Core: Shattered\].\
\
'Even a shattered one pulled a talent this cracked?' Wren thought, a grin spreading across her face. 'Hell yeah, keeping this.'\
\
She tucked the crystal core back into her inventory slot.\
\
Checking her status and rolling her talent had already eaten up a lot of time. The Beginner's Grace Period was only three days long.\
\
She had to hoard enough supplies during this window to survive the brutal Hard Mode mechanics kicking in on day four.\
\
Looking at her pitiful 4 points of Stamina, Wren sighed. She needed to find food, and fast.\
\
Glancing at the holographic screen, she saw it was 10:00 AM. She checked the regional chat feed next.\
\
Thanks to the grace period limiting everyone to three messages a day, the chat wasn't flying by at lightning speed anymore.\
\
\[I'm starving to death over here! Anyone nearby got some spare grub?\]\
\
\[How are you already starving? Didn't you open your starter pack?\]\
\
\[Yeah, are six hardtacks not enough to fill you up, bro?\]\
\
\[Wait, six hardtacks? I only got a single pack of toast! What the hell is your Luck stat to pull that much food?\]\
\
Reading the exchange, Wren immediately pulled her own starter pack from her inventory.\
\
It was a flat tin box that didn't look like it could fit six hardtacks at all.\
\
System: \[Open Starter Pack?\]\
\
Wren: \[Yes\]\
\
\[Acquired: Hardtack x3, Toast x2, Bottled Water x8, Workbench x1, Tier-C Dagger (Durability 70) x1\]\
\
Looking at her haul and connecting it to the chat, Wren figured the quantity and rarity of the starter loot depended heavily on a player's Luck stat.\
\
As she accepted the items, the tin box dissolved from her hands, and the gear slipped straight into her inventory.\
\
Lucky players scored a bellyful of rations. Unlucky ones ended up with random junk like toilet paper or hair ties.\
\
It wasn't that those things were completely useless. But right now, with everyone starving in a danger zone, a slice of bread was infinitely more valuable than a hair tie.\
\
She pulled out a hardtack, took a bite, and squinted up at the ten o'clock sky. It was brilliant, clear, and perfectly cloudless.\
\
Looking back down, she pulled up the survival manual to check the daylight hours.\
\
\[Daybreak Meadow Zone: 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM\
\
\[Briarpatch Zone: 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM\]\
\
The main screen showed she was currently in the Daybreak Meadow Zone. Since it was only ten in the morning, she had a solid eight hours of daylight left.\
\
She needed to find a spot for her Safehouse immediately. Neither the floating sphere nor the manual mentioned what happened after dark.\
\
Still, her gut was screaming at her. Getting stuck outside in an unfamiliar environment at night sounded like a total death wish.\
\
She wolfed down the rest of the hardtack in a few quick bites and clapped the crumbs off her hands. Her Stamina bumped up from 4 to 7. Time to move.\
\
Wren instantly triggered her talent.\
\
Within a 500-yard radius, a mini map bloomed in her mind, revealing loot chests, terrain changes, and massive patches of vegetation.\
\
However, there were no markers for Mutants or mutant plants. She frowned. 'Will upgrading my Talent Tier actually reveal a complete map with enemies?'\
\
The beginner tips had warned her to stay alert against all living things, plants included. Since the map couldn't track them, she had to be extra paranoid.\
\
According to her map, two loot chests sat roughly 200 yards to the west inside the Cedar Woods.\
\
Wren decided to head west, snag the chests, and then scout for a place to drop her safehouse.\
\
She tightened her backpack straps, gripped her newly unboxed dagger, and gave it a few practice swings.\
\
The survival guide ranked weapons from S down to D. Pulling a Tier-C weapon right out of the gate was an absolute win.\
\
Rocking a pair of slippers and a wild case of bedhead, Wren advanced cautiously and scanned her surroundings.\
\
Whenever she passed a sparse bush, she reached out and plucked it. Her inventory automatically vacuumed up the dropped wooden sticks.\
\
As for the dense, overgrown thickets, she didn't dare stick her hands in them.\
\
She couldn't see a thing inside. Facechecking a small Mutant was definitely not on her to do list.\
\
She covered the 200 yards in no time, arriving at the edge of the Cedar Woods. Just from foraging along the way, her inventory already held \[Wooden Stick x5\].\
\
Despite the blazing sun overhead, the woods looked pitch black inside, completely blocking out the light.\
\
Even before stepping in, a creeping chill hit her. The forest and the meadow felt like two entirely different dimensions.\
\
According to the manual, loot chests were tiered: Wood, Iron, Silver, and Gold.\
\
Right on the perimeter of the woods, Wren spotted an Iron chest. It was choked by weeds, backed against a massive cedar tree, and half buried in the dirt as if it had grown right out of the soil.\
\
About twenty feet away, a Wood chest sat half hidden behind a pile of rocks.\
\
An Iron chest was an incredibly tempting prize for a fresh spawn.\
\
But the forest felt deeply unsettling. Her survival instincts were flashing red, telling her to run.\
\
She gritted her teeth and decided to just note the coordinates. 'Safehouse first, loot later,' she reminded herself, taking a step back.\
\
A creek ran right past the Cedar Woods. She trekked about a mile and a quarter upstream until she finally found a flat clearing.\
\
It was perfect. It was close to the water, elevated enough to prevent flooding, and surrounded by plenty of timber and resources.\
\
It was the ideal spot to build.\
\
System: \[Use Wood Plank x50, Hay x60, Iron Nails x15 to build Thatch Hut (Basic)?\]\
\
Wren: \[Yes.\]\
\
\[Construction Complete: Thatch Hut (Basic)\]\
\
\[A rickety Thatch Hut: A safehouse anyone with hands could build. It isn't sturdy, but it keeps the wind and rain off your back.\]\
\
She carefully pinched the wooden door and pulled it open, making it groan with a loud, obnoxious creak.\
\
Stepping inside, she surveyed a cramped 160-square-foot floor plan. It held a rigid wooden bed and an empty window frame. That was it.\
\
Wren was highly adaptable. After a quick glance at her new real estate, she immediately shifted her focus to resource gathering.\
\
Food and water were the top priorities. Right now, her inventory held \[Hardtack x2, Toast x2, Bottled Water x8\].\
\
Even if she stretched it, that was barely two days' worth of rations.\
\
Factor in heavy manual labor, and she would burn through it even faster.\
\
Plus, outside of chests, she had no idea if there was any other reliable food source out there. She had to get that Iron loot chest, no matter what.\
\
'Besides, the Beginner's Grace Period is still active,' she reasoned with a smirk. 'Even if things get hairy, I have a flat ninety percent damage reduction.'\
\
If it was too dangerous, she could just haul ass and run.\
\
Armed with that logic, she spun on her heel, marched out of the Thatch Hut, and headed straight back toward the Cedar Woods.\
\
Chapter 3 Taming a Mutant\
\
Cedar Woods was just a short walk from the safehouse, so Wren got there in no time.\
\
Peering past the treeline, she spotted the iron loot chest sitting about forty feet into the brush.\
\
She gauged the distance, took a deep breath, and sprinted into the trees.\
\
Without warning, the chilling pressure suffocating the woods vanished abruptly. A second later, it exploded outward with ten times the intensity.\
\
The closer she got to the buried chest, the heavier that terrifying aura felt.\
\
'Holy crap,' Wren thought in a panic.\
\
She slammed on the brakes. Just as she was about to ditch the loot and run for her life, a fluffy orange-and-white rabbit plummeted from the canopy.\
\
It hit the dirt with a soft thud, landing flat on its belly right in front of her.\
\
In a blink, the oppressive terror gripping the forest totally evaporated.\
\
'Was that massive aura seriously coming from this little furball?' she wondered.\
\
Wren stared at the dizzy rabbit. Before it could shake off the fall, she grabbed it by the scruff of the neck and stuffed it into her pajama pocket. She scooped up the iron chest and hauled ass out of Cedar Woods.\
\
As she ran, the rabbit squirmed and poked its head out. It rested one tiny paw on the edge of her pocket and tilted its head in utter confusion.\
\
"Bop?" the rabbit squeaked.\
\
The moment she hugged the iron chest, her inventory system automatically absorbed it.\
\
'Thank God I'm wearing foam clogs with the heel straps engaged,' she thought mid-stride. 'If I tried sprinting in regular house slippers, I'd be a barefoot savage by now.'\
\
She was just about to clear the treeline when she remembered the wooden loot chest.\
\
'Fortune favors the bold, and cowards starve,' she reminded herself.\
\
Gritting her teeth, she pivoted and dove for the second drop. Her fingers brushed the wood, and the chest vanished into her inventory.\
\
Even though absolutely nothing was chasing them, the girl and the rabbit kept up their frantic pace. They sprinted a few hundred yards away from the woods before finally skidding to a halt.\
\
Trying to catch her breath, Wren rested one hand on her knee. She used her free hand to yank the rabbit out of her pocket, dangling it in front of her face.\
\
She gave the creature a gentle shake. The rabbit went limp like a stuffed animal, letting her swing it back and forth.\
\
Its huge, pitch-black eyes stared unblinking at her, and its nose twitched as it let out a few soft squeaks.\
\
"Bop... Bop..." the rabbit warned.\
\
"A tiny bunny that can project a boss-level aura?" Wren muttered, furrowing her brow.\
\
She wasn't stupid. The game rules explicitly warned everyone to beware of Mutants.\
\
But if this rabbit actually wanted to hurt her, it would have killed her the second she got close to its hiding spot.\
\
It wouldn't have relied on an oversized bluff only to clumsily fall out of a tree.\
\
'Oh, poor little guy,' she thought sympathetically. His stomach is completely empty. 'He must have been starving for days.'\
\
The aura had terrified her, and she figured the rabbit used that exact trick to scare off real predators.\
\
'How else would something so squishy survive out here?' More importantly, she realized she might have just stumbled onto a walking cheat code for avoiding danger.\
\
A sly smirk crept onto Wren's face. She lowered the rabbit into her palm and affectionately stroked its fur.\
\
She winced internally as she pulled out a loaf of sliced bread.\
\
There were only six slices left. She pulled one out and tentatively held it up to the bunny's nose.\
\
"You starving, little dude?" she asked softly. "Can you eat this?"\
\
The lethargic rabbit suddenly perked up. Its eyes lit up like Christmas lights. It lunged at the bread, scarfing it down in massive bites while making happy, muffled noises.\
\
"Bop... Bop, woo, Bop..." it chewed happily.\
\
Wren chuckled, letting it finish the entire slice. Watching the rabbit look totally blissed out, she reached over and poked its round belly.\
\
The bunny cooperated perfectly. It rolled over in her palm, exposing its tummy for her to pet. Wren decided to test the waters.\
\
"Can you understand me?" she asked. "If you can, jump onto this hand."\
\
She held out her empty palm. The rabbit immediately scrambled to its feet. Its hind legs kicked off, and with a blur of speed, it landed perfectly on her other hand.\
\
"Good boy," she praised.\
\
'If he understands human speech, things just got a whole lot easier,' she schemed inwardly. 'I just need to trick him into working for me.'\
\
Wren stroked the rabbit with exaggerated gentleness. She lowered her head and put on a thoroughly heartbroken expression.\
\
"Man, I really didn't score much grub today." She sighed. "And I just gave you a whole slice of bread. I honestly don't know how I'm going to survive out here."\
\
The rabbit's ears instantly shot straight up. It hopped around frantically in her palm.\
\
"What's wrong?" she asked innocently. "Do you want to come with me? Is that why you're jumping?"\
\
The bunny gave a heavy, vigorous nod.\
\
"But I can't afford a pet," she said, shaking her head. "You saw it yourself. I'm totally broke."\
\
Wren faked a sniffle, her eyes turning slightly red as she played the victim card flawlessly.\
\
'Saying I can't afford him is a total lie,' she mused. 'If one slice of bread keeps him happy, I can definitely feed him. But I wasn't lying about being broke.'\
\
Panicking, the rabbit threw its head back. That same terrifying aura surged outward as it chirped anxiously. "Bop! Bop!"\
\
Feeling the intense pressure radiating from the tiny creature, Wren couldn't stop her mouth from twitching into a smile. "Are you saying you're super useful and can help me out?"\
\
The rabbit proudly jutted out its chin. It nodded rapidly and affectionately nuzzled its furry cheek against her thumb.\
\
Overjoyed, Wren grinned broadly. "Alright then, we'll stick together." As she spoke, she gently tapped her index finger against the rabbit's forehead.\
\
Suddenly, a glowing golden emblem ignited right where her finger touched the fur. It pulsed with light.\
\
The rabbit didn't seem to notice at all, happily continuing to rub its face against her hand.\
\
System: \[Do you wish to use a Taming Stone to bind this High-Tier Mutant (Juvenile)?\]\
\
'A Taming Stone? I can actually bind this little guy?' Wren thought in shock.\
\
She immediately pulled up the survival guide and quickly found the section on Mutant classifications, which ranged from Low, Mid, and High, all the way to Elite.\
\
'Looks like this little furball is actually top-tier,' she noted with satisfaction.\
\
Wren: \[Yes.\]\
\
\[Insufficient items. Taming Stone missing. Binding failed.\]\
\
'Well, no need to rush things,' she figured.\
\
She tucked the rabbit back into her pocket and gave its head a reassuring pat. Then, she pulled the iron chest from her inventory.\
\
"We're going to skirt the edge of Cedar Woods," she told her new companion. "Bop, keep an eye out for any other Mutants nearby."\
\
"Bop" seemed like a fitting name for the squeaky little hopper.\
\
Wren didn't feel a shred of guilt about bossing around such an adorable creature.\
\
She needed to instill a solid work ethic in Bop from day one.\
\
'You eat my food and ride in my pocket, you earn your keep,' she reasoned.\
\
Wren accessed her inventory and popped open the two loot chests she had just scored.\
\
\[Opening Wooden Chest. Acquired: Bottled Water x3, Cinnamon Roll x2, Chocolate Brownie x1, Iron Nails x10\]\
\
\[Opening Iron Chest. Acquired: Bottled Water x8, Plain Bread Roll x3, Jar of Honey x1, Flint & Steel x1, Utility Gloves x1, D-Tier Iron Axe (Durability: 90) x1\]\
\
The food and water drops alone were enough to keep her going for a solid stretch. Wren materialized the utility gloves and slipped them on.\
\
She gripped the iron axe and headed downstream with Bop in tow.\
\
Her mental map flagged another loot chest buried deep within Cedar Woods, but she completely wrote it off.\
\
It was way too risky. If things went south in the deep timber, she would never make it out alive. Instead, she stuck to the creek banks.\
\
She planned to chop some wood along the way and scavenge whatever else she could find.\
\
Even knowing the terrifying aura was just Bop faking it, her gut screamed that the woods were bad news.\
\
She decided to wait until she snagged some serious firepower before exploring the interior.\
\
Being thrust into an alien wilderness meant playing it incredibly safe for now.\
\
After hiking a few hundred yards, Wren finally spotted a pair of solitary oak trees.\
\
Energized, she jogged over, hefted her new axe, and took a massive swing. The blade merely chipped the bark, leaving a pathetic surface scratch.\
\
Wren stared at the tree, absolutely dumbfounded. She looked at the giant oak, then down at the Iron Axe in her hands. In total disbelief, she pulled up her character screen to double check her stats.\
\
'Is 8 Strength really this weak?' she grumbled internally. 'Or does this axe just suck?'\
\
Gritting her teeth, she accepted her harsh reality and got to work. She hacked away at the trunk, one agonizing swing at a time.\
\
It took her a grueling hour to fell both oaks. Wren leaned against a stump, panting heavily. She checked her gear.\
\
The Iron Axe was down to 80 durability, and all she had to show for her backbreaking labor was Wood x4 in her inventory.\
\
Her Stamina had also dropped by a point. Feeling parched, she pulled out a bottle of water. She cupped her hand to let Bop lap up a few mouthfuls, then chugged the rest.\
\
Wiping her mouth, she grabbed her gear and readied herself to keep moving.\
\
Right at that moment, Bop popped his head out of her pocket. He let out a low, warning growl toward the path ahead.\
\
"Bop... Bop..." the rabbit warned.\
\
Wren instantly dropped the axe into her inventory and drew her dagger. She slipped into a defensive stance, her eyes locked onto the dense, rustling brush just ahead of them.\
\
Chapter 4 Hunting Mutants and Heading Home\
\
Keeping her eyes glued to the brush, Wren slowly backed away.\
\
'I need to boost my willpower and upgrade Seeker's Sight right now,' she realized with a sinking feeling. 'Flying blind without a minimap is basically a death sentence, and relying solely on Bop is pushing my reflexes way too hard.'\
\
She barely managed a few steps before a sharp rustling broke the silence. A vibrant green snake slithered out of the foliage.\
\
Its crimson eyes pinned her down as it coiled tightly, flicking a blood red tongue and letting out a nasty warning hiss.\
\
Then it hit her. She still had that sweet ninety percent damage immunity from the three day beginner protection.\
\
Wren stopped retreating. She tightened her grip and aimed her blade dead at the reptile.\
\
The snake instantly cut its hiss short and arched into a strike.\
\
The moment it launched itself like a coiled spring, Wren threw herself sideways, tumbling hard across the grass.\
\
Right on cue, Bop unleashed a terrifying aura from inside her pocket. The snake felt the overwhelming pressure and instantly canceled its follow up strike.\
\
It whipped its head around, desperate to bolt back into the weeds.\
\
Wren scrambled up. With lethal precision, she drove her dagger right into the base of the snake's skull.\
\
She dragged the blade downward in one brutal motion. The underbelly ripped open, spraying a fountain of neon purple blood.\
\
Mortally wounded, the snake thrashed wildly. It desperately tried to reach safety, but the embedded blade pinned it down. When the snake whipped its head back for a final desperate bite,\
\
Wren simply yanked the dagger free and drove it straight down through its skull.\
\
System: \[Low Green Viper slain. Rewards: 1x Wooden Chest, 3x Snake Meat, 1x Snake Gallbladder, 1x Green Viper Venom.\
\
\[Green Viper Venom: A mild toxin, but potent enough to completely paralyze a target.\]\
\
\[Congratulations! You unlocked the Mutant Hunter achievement. Achievement Points +1. Rewards: 1x Iron Chest, 10x Iron Ingots.\]\
\
\[Regional First! You are the first player in Sector 47 to complete the Mutant Hunter achievement. Bonus Rewards: 1x Achievement Point, 1x Iron Chest, 1x Unallocated Stat Point.\]\
\
'An achievement bonus?' Wren thought, her eyes widening in surprise.\
\
She pulled up her profile. On the leaderboard, she and some guy named Connor Hayes were tied for first place in the entire sector.\
\
They both had two achievement points, and nobody else was even on the radar yet.\
\
It looked like the first player to hit a milestone grabbed the standard loot, but only the regional trailblazer scored the bonus rewards.\
\
Loot chests were easy enough to farm. That unallocated stat point, however, was absolute gold. It was her only ticket to boosting her Willpower and upgrading Seeker's Sight.\
\
Suddenly fired up to grind for more resources, Wren gave Bop's fuzzy head an enthusiastic rub. She pumped her fist, totally hyping up her pet with pure gamer energy.\
\
"Hell yeah, Bop! You are the real MVP," Wren cheered, flashing a massive grin. "Awesome teamwork back there. Thanks for the heads up. Let's keep this momentum rolling and I will hook you up with some sweet rolls tonight!"\
\
Bop scratched happily at her pocket, letting out an excited chirp.\
\
Staring down at the little guy, Wren just could not wrap her head around it. 'How on earth is this harmless little bunny classified as a High-Grade Mutant? The killer snake I just gutted was only a Low Grade.'\
\
'Well, no use overthinking it,' she concluded with a shrug.\
\
She dumped her shiny new stat point straight into Willpower, bumping it up to 21. Checking the time, she noticed it was already noon.\
\
Her Stamina was sitting at a measly 5. She dug a piece of hardtack out of her inventory, broke off a crumbly piece of the crust for Bop, and wolfed down the rest.\
\
Over the next two hours, Wren did not run into a single mutant. No new loot chests popped up on her mental radar, either.\
\
Still, she refused to slack off. Rocking her Utility Gloves, she stripped the surrounding brush and gathered dry grass as she hiked.\
\
\[Acquired: 15x Wooden Sticks, 20x Dry Hay.\]\
\
After a massive trek, a loot chest finally flickered onto her map to the northwest. Knowing she had to be back at the Safehouse by six o'clock, she broke into a light jog.\
\
She would much rather be early than risk getting locked out in the dark.\
\
Arriving at the exact coordinates, Wren stopped and scratched her head. The patch of grass was completely empty.\
\
'Where is the chest?' she wondered, totally stumped.\
\
The map insisted it was right here. She paced around the marked zone, finding nothing but weeds. 'Is the map glitching?' she thought, frowning.\
\
That felt unlikely, considering how accurate it had been all morning.\
\
'Wait, maybe it is not on the ground,' she realized with a gasp. 'Maybe it is under it!'\
\
No time to waste. Wren summoned her Crafting Bench.\
\
\[Crafting Bench: Place materials to craft items. There are no uncraftable items, only players lacking materials.\]\
\
She quickly flipped through her tutorial for a shovel recipe. It just took two pieces of wood.\
\
She tossed them onto the bench, and a crisp chime echoed in her head.\
\
\[Crafting Successful: 1x Tier-D Wooden Shovel (Durability: 50)\]\
\
Wren picked up the wooden shovel and gave it an experimental swing. The weight was solid and totally manageable.\
\
Time was ticking. Wiping the sweat from her forehead, Wren drove the shovel into the dirt.\
\
Out here, far from the stream, the ground was packed hard. Forty minutes of backbreaking labor later, her shovel finally hit something solid.\
\
She carefully cleared away the loose dirt, revealing a Wooden Chest.\
\
She tapped the lid, and the chest vanished straight into her inventory. Wren blinked, spotting two earthworms writhing in the dirt right where the box had been.\
\
Thanks to this world's crazy ecosystem, these bugs were easily three times fatter than anything back on Earth.\
\
They looked half crushed and tangled together, obviously squished by the heavy chest.\
\
Kneeling down, Wren scooped them out of the hole. Channeling her inner survivalist, she chucked them into her bag.\
\
\[Acquired: 2x Earthworms\]\
\
\[Earthworms: Can be used to craft Low-Grade Fishing Bait.\]\
\
After stashing the bait, she downed a bottle of water and checked the time.\
\
It was already three in the afternoon. With only three hours left until curfew, she could not afford to push any further.\
\
She was miles away from the safehouse and really needed to hustle back.\
\
Luckily, she had Seeker's Sight. Even though the radar capped at 500 yards, she could easily retrace her steps by locking onto landmarks.\
\
Plus, her inventory was totally packed. Even if she had the time, she literally had no space left.\
\
Thinking about the four loot chests sitting in her bag, Wren craved that sweet dopamine rush of unboxing them.\
\
She shifted into high gear and power walked toward the safehouse.\
\
She ignored the stray materials along the way. With a tight three hour window, getting home was the absolute priority. Min maxing a few extra sticks was definitely not worth risking her life.\
\
On the trek back, Wren thoughtfully snapped off a few large, soft leaves from a nearby tree. She planned to build a proper bed for Bop.\
\
She could handle sleeping on that stiff wood plank bed, but her tiny companion deserved a cozy nest.\
\
The duo pushed hard, finally making it back to the Safehouse just before the sun dipped.\
\
Wren slipped inside the thatch hut and slammed the flimsy latch shut. Standing safely inside her base, she let out a massive sigh of relief.\
\
Checking the system interface, she noted there were exactly twenty minutes left until lockdown.\
\
After a brutally exhausting day, she could finally kick back and rest.\
\
Chapter 5 Facing the Night\
\
Wren flopped onto the mattress with a heavy sigh and stretched her aching limbs.\
\
Bop scrambled out of her pocket and immediately collapsed into a furry pancake. The little rabbit looked completely drained from their day out in the wasteland.\
\
Lying on the wooden cot, Wren absentmindedly stroked Bop's soft ears and stared at the ceiling. The straw woven overhead was so thin it practically let the starlight through.\
\
That made her increasingly uneasy about her new shelter.\
\
'What kind of safehouse is literally called a Thatch Hut?' she wondered silently. It sounded completely unreliable.\
\
She pulled up the interface to check the upgrade requirements.\
\
\[Thatch Hut (Basic) to Thatch Hut (Advanced) Upgrade Requirements: Wood Plank x60, Thatch x80, Iron Nails x30\]\
\
Hay was easy enough to get by clearing bushes. Iron nails were manufactured items, and she was not sure if they only dropped from loot chests.\
\
As for wood planks, they were obviously crafted from the raw timber she chopped earlier today.\
\
She opened the Survival Tutorial to search the crafting database.\
\
\[Iron Nails can be crafted at the workbench using Iron Ingots. 1 Iron Ingot yields 10 Iron Nails.\]\
\
\[Wood Planks can be crafted at the workbench using Wood. 1 Wood yields 4 Wood Planks.\]\
\
She did the math in her head. 'That means the ten iron ingots I got from today's achievement will make a hundred nails,' she thought happily.\
\
As for the wood, she would just have to keep chopping down trees.\
\
Done worrying about the safehouse, Wren scooped Bop up and set him aside. She sat up with a surge of energy and pulled her newly acquired loot chests from her inventory.\
\
Two were wooden and two were iron.\
\
She rubbed her hands together and grinned. 'Finally, it was time for the main event. Let the unboxing begin!'\
\
To Bop, Wren looked like she was putting on a bizarre mime routine. He watched her pull invisible objects out of thin air and place them on the mattress.\
\
He let out a thoroughly confused squeak.\
\
Wren noticed the little guy staring blankly at her empty hands. "Bop?" she asked, tilting her head.\
\
She picked up one of the wooden chests and waved it gently in front of his nose. "Hey buddy, can you see what this is?" she asked with a curious smile.\
\
Bop tilted his head, bunched his hind legs, and lunged straight at the wooden chest.\
\
Wren didn't even have time to pull it away. The rabbit shot forward like a tiny cannonball. Instead of colliding with the chest, he passed right through it as if it were made of air.\
\
He landed back on the mattress with a series of confused hops.\
\
Wren's eyes widened as she gripped the chest. It felt perfectly solid in her hands. A realization struck her.\
\
'So Bop can't see or touch the loot chests, but he can see and eat the food that comes out of them?' she reasoned silently.\
\
This chest probably wasn't a native product of this world. Otherwise, a local creature like Bop would definitely be able to see it.\
\
Hearing Bop continue to chatter in confusion, Wren pulled a cinnamon roll from her bag. She placed it on a broad leaf she had brought inside and nudged it toward him. It was best to distract him with a sweet treat.\
\
Seeing the rabbit instantly dig in with pure joy, Wren let out a breath of relief.\
\
If he kept pestering her about the invisible box, she would have a terrible time trying to explain it.\
\
It was time to focus on the chests. Wren wiped her palms on her pajamas, clasped her hands together, and closed her eyes.\
\
She sent up a quick prayer to the gaming gods. 'Come on, RNG Jesus, bless me with that top tier luck! Let's see some good drops!'\
\
After finishing her little ritual, she tapped the screen to open the two wooden loot chests.\
\
System: \[Open Wooden Chest x2?\]\
\
Wren: \[Yes.\]\
\
\[Received: Bottled Water x8, Plain Bread Roll x4, Toast x2, Cheese Danish x1, Vacuum-Sealed Meat Stick x1, Honey Buns x2, Crew Socks x1, Men's Tank Top x1, Candles x5\]\
\
Because her inventory slots were totally maxed out, the auto loot system failed. Instead, a small mountain of items materialized and spilled across the wooden bed in a chaotic heap.\
\
Bop had been burying his face in his cinnamon roll, but he happened to look up.\
\
His eyes went wide, and he practically froze. Pure shock washed over him.\
\
'Holy cow, food! Look at all that grub!' the rabbit thought wildly.\
\
Drool nearly pooled in his mouth as he looked down at his half eaten roll, then back up at the glorious pile of supplies.\
\
Without a shred of hesitation, he straightened up and bolted toward the feast.\
\
'What kind of miserable life was I living before this? Where did all this amazing stuff come from?!' he wondered eagerly.\
\
Just as Bop was about to dive headfirst into the pile, Wren snatched him by the scruff of his neck. She lifted him into the air and gave his tiny forehead a gentle flick.\
\
"Ah-ah, hands off, buddy," she scolded lightly. "These are our emergency rations. If you want more treats, you have to work hard and help me out. No free rides in the apocalypse."\
\
Hearing her words, Bop let his perked ears droop. He let out a pathetic, whimpering whine. "Bop, boooop," he cried sadly.\
\
She set him back down in front of his cinnamon roll. The poor guy looked so depressed that he chewed his food with a tragic, long face.\
\
Wren thought back to how Bop had instantly warned her about the mutant earlier, and how well he had coordinated with her to kill the green snake.\
\
She picked up the cheese danish, which was the only premium treat from the wooden chests. She broke it in half and placed a piece on his leaf.\
\
She gently stroked his fluffy fur. "Alright, this half is a bonus for spotting that danger today. Good job, Bop."\
\
The moment Bop saw the pastry, his gloomy mood vanished into thin air.\
\
He did a joyful little hop onto Wren's lap, rubbing his tiny paws against her pants in pure gratitude.\
\
Message delivered, he leaped back onto his leaf and buried his nose right back into his dinner.\
\
Wren popped the other half of the cheese danish into her mouth. She watched her status bar change as she chewed, noting that she gained one Stamina point.\
\
Realizing she had only eaten two pieces of hardtack and two bottles of water all day, she pulled out the slice of toast she had saved earlier.\
\
She wolfed it down along with a bottle of water. Her Stamina climbed back up to eight.\
\
She reminded herself to keep a close eye on her Stamina from now on. If it dropped below two, she would get hit with the Sluggish debuff.\
\
She wasn't entirely sure what Sluggish felt like, but it probably meant moving in slow motion.\
\
Wren shook her head. 'A debuff like that definitely couldn't be good.'\
\
Since her Seeker's Sight couldn't detect mutants yet, she had to rely entirely on Bop for early warnings. That meant she needed to treat him well.\
\
However, future chest openings definitely needed to happen out of his sight.\
\
He couldn't see the chests themselves, but he sure could see the loot.\
\
With her current food supply, she could afford to feed him well. But she didn't want him associating chest openings with free handouts.\
\
He needed to understand the golden rule of the wasteland. No work meant no food.\
\
Wren checked her inventory again and found it completely overflowing. She pulled up both the workbench and the Survival Tutorial to see if she could craft a storage container to clear some space.\
\
\[Small Storage Crate can be crafted at the workbench using Wood. 1 Wood yields 1 Small Storage Crate. 2 Wood yields 1 Large Storage Crate.\
\
\[Small Storage Crate Capacity: 20 slots. Large Storage Crate Capacity: 50 slots.\]\
\
She only had two pieces of wood left in her inventory, so she absolutely had to craft a crate today.\
\
This thatch hut was already tiny. If she piled everything on the floor, she wouldn't even have room to step.\
\
Wren stared at the recipe and rubbed her chin. A thought crossed her mind. 'The small crate gives twenty slots, but the large one gives fifty.\
\
'I might as well go big to save resources and get more space.'\
\
System: \[Spend Wood x2 to craft a Large Storage Crate?\]\
\
Wren: \[Yes.\]\
\
\[Crafting Successful.\]\
\
A sturdy, square wooden crate materialized in front of her. Wren swept everything off the bed and neatly packed it inside.\
\
She also stored everything from her inventory except for some basic food, water, the workbench, her axe, and her dagger.\
\
Sitting back on the wooden cot, she turned her gaze toward the window.\
\
A massive shadow was creeping across the land, swallowing the final rays of light. The inside of the thatch hut rapidly grew dim and cold.\
\
The inside of the thatch hut rapidly grew dim and cold.\
\
Night had finally fallen.\
\
Chapter 6 World Chat and Friend Requests\
\
Wren pulled out the candle she had just looted and lit it with her flint.\
\
She decided to pop open her last two iron loot chests right inside her storage box. That way, Bop wouldn't see the goods.\
\
System: \[Open iron loot chest x2?\]\
\
Wren: \[Yes.\]\
\
\[Loot Acquired: bottled water x14, plain bread rolls x2, sliced bread x3, honey buns x6, sack of oats x1, vanilla cake roll x1, smoked salmon x1, electrolyte potion x2, fleece blanket x1, women's undergarments x1, candles x6\]\
\
'Wow, the drop rate for water is actually pretty crazy,' Wren thought, raising an eyebrow at her new stash.\
\
She transferred the fresh supplies into her storage and took a quick inventory of all the food she had split between the box and her backpack.\
\
\[Bottled water x39, hardtack x1, sliced bread x4, cinnamon roll x1, chocolate brownie x1, plain bread rolls x9, jar of honey x1, vacuum-sealed meat stick x1, honey buns x8, sack of oats x1, vanilla cake roll x1, smoked salmon x1, and raw snake meat x3.\]\
\
Aside from the raw snake meat that needed roasting over a fire, everything else was completely ready to eat.\
\
After wrapping up her inventory management, Wren let out a long breath. She tucked her backpack away, grabbed her new blanket, and climbed into bed.\
\
The second her body fully relaxed from a hard day of manual labor, her leg muscles screamed in protest.\
\
She massaged her thighs and ran through a quick full-body stretching routine on the mattress, then leaned back against the wall.\
\
Her safehouse was still a bit flimsy, and the candlelight flickered dimly. Over in the corner, Bop was sprawled out on a cozy bed of soft leaves.\
\
Wren opened the world chat to do some digital surfing and see what the other players in her zone were talking about.\
\
The three-message daily limit effectively kept the feed from turning into an unreadable blur.\
\
What really made her stomach drop was the player count in the top right corner. The starting population of one million from that morning had already plummeted to just under 900,000.\
\
It was only day one, and over a hundred thousand people were already dead. This was happening even with the ninety percent damage immunity from the beginner's grace period.\
\
Once that three-day safety net vanished, the casualty rate was going to skyrocket.\
\
'Upgrading my safehouse and gearing up isn't just a priority anymore,' Wren realized with a frown. 'It's do or die.'\
\
\[I wanna go home,\] one user pleaded in the chat. \[I want to go back to Earth. Can somebody please take me home?\]\
\
\[Thank God for the beginner's grace period. I ran into a rabid porcupine today. If it weren't for the damage reduction, I'd totally be one of those dead guys.\]\
\
\[Anybody adding friends? We should party up, support each other, and share survival tips.\]\
\
\[What am I supposed to do? I'm gonna run out of starter pack food by tomorrow. If I don't find a loot chest soon, I'm toast!\]\
\
\[To the guy crying about going home. Drop the delusions. Open your eyes and look at how many people Zone 47 has lost. You actually still think Earth is an option?\]\
\
\[A wooden loot chest literally fell out of a tree while I was chopping it down. Why are these things hidden in the weirdest spots? Worst part is, it barely had any food inside.\]\
\
\[Dude above me has insane luck. Has anyone else actually found a loot chest? Somebody posted a picture of a wooden one this afternoon.\
\
\[Has anyone found an iron one yet? What does it even look like?\]\
\
Right at that moment, a player named Caleb Wright posted a picture of an iron loot chest in the chat. The message feed immediately blew up, scrolling at warp speed.\
\
\[Holy crap, we got a pro over here!\]\
\
\[I couldn't even find a wooden chest today, and this guy is already cracking open iron ones?\]\
\
\[Hey boss, what's inside an iron chest? How much better is the loot compared to the wooden ones?\]\
\
\[Add me, bro!\]\
\
\[Forget about it. His friend requests are probably maxed out by now.\]\
\
\[Drop your coordinates, man. Let me carry your bags!\]\
\
Amidst the flood of messages, Caleb popped back into the chat.\
\

I almost didn't go to my granddaughter's piano recital.
She's 7 years old. Her name is Amaya. She has been practicing the same Beethoven piece for 4 months on the upright in her mother's living room, the one with the sticky middle C, and she was going to play it in front of 60 people in the auditorium at Springhill Elementary on a Thursday night in March, and her grandmother almost stayed home.
I sat in my bedroom in my best blue dress with my purse on my lap and I told my husband Cornell to go on without me. He turned around in the doorway with his tie half knotted and he said, "Loretta. What are you doing."
I said, "My pressure is up. I can feel it. I don't want to make a scene."
He looked at me for a long time. Then he said, "Loretta. She's going to look for you in that crowd."
And I sat on the edge of the bed and I cried.
Because I was 63 years old and I was scared to sit in an auditorium full of people for 90 minutes because I was afraid my body was going to embarrass me in front of my own grandbaby.
My name is Loretta. I live in Mobile, Alabama, off Spring Hill Avenue, in the same little brick house Cornell and I bought in 1991 when our oldest was 4. I worked 31 years as a kindergarten teacher in the Mobile County school system. I retired in 2022. I have three children and 6 grandchildren and the youngest of them, Amaya, is the one who calls me on FaceTime every Sunday after church to show me her piano hands.
And on a Thursday night in March 2024, I almost missed her first recital because my blood pressure had been climbing for two years and the pills my doctor gave me weren't holding it down anymore.
Let me back up.
I was diagnosed with high blood pressure when I was 54. Doctor Whitfield at the clinic on Airport Boulevard, the one with the parking lot you can never find a spot in, he took my pressure twice on a Tuesday morning and he said, "Mrs. Loretta, your top number is 162. We need to put you on something."
I didn't argue. My mama died of a stroke at 71. My daddy had two heart attacks before he was 65. I knew what runs in our family. I took the lisinopril and I started walking three mornings a week and I cut back on the salt and I thought I was doing what I was supposed to do.
For a few years, it held. Numbers came down. Not great, but better. The doctor was happy.
Then about two years ago, somewhere around 61, it started creeping back. He upped the lisinopril. Added a water pill. The numbers came down for a minute and then crept back. He added a third medication, a calcium channel blocker, and the side effects started. My ankles swelled up like sausages by 4 in the afternoon. My head felt thick. I started getting dizzy when I stood up from the couch.
I'd go for my checkups and the cuff would beep and Cornell would be sitting in the chair across from me and I'd watch his face change when the numbers came up on the little screen. 156 over 94. 162 over 98. 168 over 101.
Doctor Whitfield would shake his head and adjust the prescription and say, "Loretta, sometimes the body just doesn't want to cooperate. We'll keep working on it."
Keep working on it. Like my pressure was a stubborn child in his classroom.
But the thing nobody talks about with blood pressure is what it does to you between the appointments. Not the numbers. The fear.
I started feeling it in my chest at random times. A heaviness. A pressure behind my eyes when I bent down to tie my shoes. I'd be at the grocery store reaching for a can of crushed tomatoes on the top shelf and a wave of something would come over me and I'd have to grab the cart handle and wait for it to pass.
I stopped going to the Thursday night Bible study at Mount Olive because the church is on the third floor of the family life center and the elevator is slow and I started worrying about getting stuck in it.
I stopped going to my sister Vernita's apartment because it's two flights up and by the time I got to her door I was breathing like I'd run a mile.
I started saying no to things. Not big things, at first. Just little things. The Saturday cookout at my brother in law's. The hair appointment with Miss Yvonne who I'd been seeing since 1998. My friend Patrice's birthday dinner at Wintzell's downtown.
I told everyone I was just tired. Cornell knew. He knew because he'd come home and find me sitting in the recliner in the dark with the TV off, just sitting there, listening to my own heart.
And then Amaya's recital came up.
My daughter Tanya called me three weeks ahead to remind me. She'd already called me two times before that. She knew, the way daughters know, that I'd been pulling back. She said, "Mama. Amaya is asking when you're coming. She wants to know what color dress you're wearing so she can match her ribbon."
I told her I'd be there. I bought the blue dress at Dillard's that weekend. I had my hair done on the Wednesday before. I planned it out the way you plan out a trip to a foreign country, every step, every parking lot, every bathroom, every chair.
And the morning of the recital my pressure cuff at home read 171 over 103 and I sat down on the edge of the tub in my bathroom and I thought, "I cannot do this. I cannot sit in that crowd for 90 minutes with my pressure like this. What if something happens? In front of all those people? In front of Amaya?"
That's why I was sitting on the edge of the bed with my purse on my lap.
Cornell stood in the doorway with his tie half knotted and he didn't say anything for a minute. Then he came over and he sat down next to me and he put his hand on my back and he said, "Loretta. We're going. I'll drive slow. You sit in the back row by the door. If you need to step out, you step out. But she's looking for you. We're going."
I went. I sat in the back row. I held Cornell's hand so hard I left half moons in his palm with my fingernails. Amaya played her Beethoven and she missed two notes and she kept going and at the end she stood up and bowed and she looked into that crowd and she found me. She found me in the back row. And she waved. A little wave. Just for her grandmama.
I cried in the parking lot. I cried in the car. I cried in the driveway when we got home.
Because I had spent 90 minutes scared. I had spent 90 minutes with my hand on my chest. I had spent 90 minutes calculating how fast I could get to the exit. And my granddaughter, my baby, had stood on that stage and looked for me and I should have been the proudest woman in that room and instead I was the most afraid.
That night, after Cornell went to bed, I sat at the kitchen table in my robe and I opened up the laptop and I started looking.
I had spent two years doing what my doctor told me to do. Three medications. Low salt. Walking. Weight down 12 pounds. And my numbers were worse than the day I started. And I had just sat through my grandbaby's recital with my hand on my chest.
I wasn't looking to replace the medication. I wasn't trying to be one of those people who throws away her pills and trusts the universe. I was a kindergarten teacher. I believe in science. But I was looking for what my doctor wasn't telling me.
I typed in things like "why isn't my blood pressure medication working" and "what doctors don't explain about hypertension." I went down a rabbit hole that started on a regular health website and ended somewhere I didn't expect.
I found an article about the inside of your blood vessels.
I didn't know your blood vessels had an inside. I mean, I knew they were tubes, but I didn't know there was a living layer on the inside of those tubes that does work. It's called the endothelium, and it's not just a wall. It's a living membrane that controls whether your blood vessels stay tight or whether they relax. It does this by producing a molecule called nitric oxide. When the endothelium is healthy and functioning properly, it produces plenty of nitric oxide, your vessels relax, blood flows freely, and your pressure stays where it ought to be.
But years of inflammation, stress, processed food, and just plain getting older wear that inner wall down. When the wall isn't functioning properly, it can't produce as much nitric oxide. So your vessels stay tight. Blood forces its way through. That's high blood pressure. And the harder the blood pushes through tight vessels, the more it stresses the wall, which makes it worse, which raises the pressure more. A cycle that feeds itself.
I sat at the kitchen table reading that and I felt something I hadn't felt in two years.
I felt like somebody was finally telling me what was wrong with me.
Because every pill I'd been taking, the lisinopril, the water pill, the calcium channel blocker, they all force your vessels open from the outside or pull fluid out of you. None of them touch the wall. The wall keeps deteriorating underneath. Which is why the medications stopped working over time. Which is why my doctor kept "adjusting" them. Which is why I was sitting in the back row at my granddaughter's recital scared.
The article mentioned a few things that had been studied for supporting the function of that inner wall. Most of them were ingredients I'd never heard of. But one of them I had heard of.
Amla.
A little green fruit from India. Indian gooseberry. They've been using it for thousands of years in Ayurvedic medicine. The article said it contains compounds called emblicanins that have been studied for their role in supporting endothelial function, the function of that inner wall. When the wall is supported and functioning better, it can start producing more of its own nitric oxide, the way it did when you were younger. Vessels can relax more naturally. Pressure on the walls can ease.
It wasn't a drug. It wasn't forcing anything. It was supporting the part of your body that's supposed to regulate your pressure in the first place.
I want to be careful here. I'm not telling you I read one article and ran out and changed my whole life. I read articles for three weeks. I read about the research. I read about the studies. I read about what amla was and what it wasn't. I called my niece Brittany, who is a nurse practitioner in Atlanta, and I asked her what she thought. She said she'd been recommending amla to some of her patients for over a year as part of a broader plan. She said the research on the vascular side was real, even if it wasn't going to make the evening news.
She said something I'll never forget. She said, "Aunt Loretta, the medications you're taking force your vessels open. They don't fix the reason your vessels are tight in the first place. Amla works further upstream. It supports the wall itself. That's a different conversation."
A different conversation.
That's what I'd been wanting for two years. A different conversation.
I ordered a bottle from Auniva that night. It was 4 days before it arrived. Brown box on the porch when I came back from the mailbox.
I told Cornell I was going to try something. I didn't make a big speech about it. I just told him. He looked at the bottle. He read the label. He said, "Loretta, you're a grown woman. You do what you think is right."
I started taking two capsules every morning with my coffee. I did not stop my medications. I did not change anything else. I just added the amla and I kept doing what I was doing. I told my niece and she told me to track my numbers every morning so I'd have something to look at.
The first week, nothing changed. I expected nothing. I'd been on lisinopril for 9 years. I knew bodies don't turn on a dime.
The second week, my morning numbers came down a few points. Could've been anything. I wrote it down.
The third week, my ankles weren't as swollen at the end of the day. I noticed it when I was putting on my house slippers. The little dent the elastic leaves in my ankle was lighter.
The fourth week, I walked from my car to the grocery store entrance at Winn Dixie and I didn't have to stop to catch my breath halfway. I stood in the produce section and I picked up a cantaloupe and I realized, in that moment, that I had stopped doing this calculation in my head. The calculation of how far I could walk before I had to rest. The calculation of where the nearest place to sit was. I had been doing that calculation, all day, every day, for almost two years, and that afternoon at Winn Dixie I had walked all the way to the produce section without doing it.
I bought the cantaloupe. I bought some greens. I walked back to my car. And I sat in the driver's seat in the parking lot and I called Cornell.
